description: This bar chart illustrates the distribution of samples across different reasoning categories. The horizontal axis represents the reasoning category, labeled with “Mathematical Reasoning”, “General Reasoning”, “Natural Scene Reasoning”, “Physical Reasoning”, “Logical Reasoning”, and “Chemical Reasoning” in that order, and appears to be categorical with no explicit sorting. The vertical axis is labeled “Number of Samples” and uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10⁴, with tick labels at intervals of powers of 10. There are six light blue bars, one for each reasoning category. The “Mathematical Reasoning” bar is the tallest, extending to approximately 1709 samples. The “General Reasoning” bar reaches approximately 413 samples, while the “Natural Scene Reasoning” bar extends to approximately 232 samples. The “Physical Reasoning” bar reaches approximately 91 samples, the “Logical Reasoning” bar extends to approximately 49 samples, and the shortest bar, representing “Chemical Reasoning”, reaches approximately 49 samples. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
